prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs address blocking/backpressure caused by the write_stream memory object stream being created with buffer size 0 in stdio_server(). A size-0 (rendezvous) channel forces send() to block until stdout_writer is ready to receive, which causes a handler trying to queue a final response to block while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 exposes read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as caller-supplied parameters (default 0, so out-of-the-box behavior is unchanged and callers must know to opt in). #2654 hardcodes the write_stream buffer to 1, fixing the blocking behavior by default, and ships a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the progress-notification-blocks-response scenario. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs address blocking/backpressure caused by the write_stream memory object stream being created with buffer size 0 in stdio_server(). prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: the WWW-Authenticate header was parsed with naive string/regex matching that didn't respect quoted values or comma boundaries, causing substring matches on parameter/scheme names (e.g. matching part of a param name, or picking up params across different auth-scheme challenges) instead of matching complete, correctly-scoped tokens. Both add a quote-aware, comma-splitting parser to replace the old approach, touching the exact same function/region of the same file and would conflict on merge. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3041's parser (_split_www_authenticate_segments + _extract_bearer_auth_params) explicitly identifies the Bearer challenge by its scheme token before collecting params, so it correctly excludes params belonging to a different challenge when a header contains multiple comma-separated challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer realm=y'). 3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips text up to the first space and treats everything after as one flat param list, which does not isolate the Bearer challenge in multi-challenge headers, making it a narrower fix for the same root cause.

clusters.pick_reason: 2654 changes the default write_stream buffer from 0 to 1, so the fix applies to every caller of stdio_server() without requiring extra arguments; 2215's configurable parameters default to 0, leaving the original blocking behavior in place unless a caller explicitly opts in, which most existing call sites (that invoke stdio_server() with no args) never will. 2654 also adds a targeted regression test (BlockingStdout in test_stdio.py) that reproduces the progress-notification-blocks-final-response scenario, whereas 2215's test changes are not shown to cover that failure mode directly.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both PRs address blocking/backpressure caused by the write_stream memory object stream being created with buffer size 0 in stdio_server(). A size-0 (rendezvous) channel forces send() to block until stdout_writer is ready to receive, which causes a handler trying to queue a final response to block while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 exposes read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as caller-supplied parameters (default 0, so out-of-the-box behavior is unchanged and callers must know to opt in). #2654 hardcodes the write_stream buffer to 1, fixing the blocking behavior by default, and ships a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the progress-notification-blocks-response scenario.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 fixes the failure at its source inside _handle_reconnection: it correlates the error to the specific pending request via ctx.session_message (only errors out the JSONRPCRequest tied to the broken resumption stream) by sending a JSONRPCError with INTERNAL_ERROR through ctx.read_stream_writer, and it removes the '# pragma no cover' marker on the max-attempts branch, indicating the branch now has test coverage. #3098's shown diff does not touch _handle_reconnection itself; it adds a generic _unwrap_exception helper to pull a StreamableHTTPError out of an anyio ExceptionGroup, which would surface the failure as a session-wide exception (propagated via the TaskGroup) rather than a per-request JSON-RPC error, affecting all in-flight requests instead of only the one whose stream disconnected.

clusters.pick_reason: 3041's parser (_split_www_authenticate_segments + _extract_bearer_auth_params) explicitly identifies the Bearer challenge by its scheme token before collecting params, so it correctly excludes params belonging to a different challenge when a header contains multiple comma-separated challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer realm=y'). 3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips text up to the first space and treats everything after as one flat param list, which does not isolate the Bearer challenge in multi-challenge headers, making it a narrower fix for the same root cause.

clusters.pick_reason: 2654 changes the default write_stream buffer from 0 to 1, so the fix applies to every caller of stdio_server() without requiring extra arguments; 2215's configurable parameters default to 0, leaving the original blocking behavior in place unless a caller explicitly opts in, which most existing call sites (that invoke stdio_server() with no args) never will. 2654 also adds a targeted regression test (BlockingStdout in test_stdio.py) that reproduces the progress-notification-blocks-final-response scenario, whereas 2215's test changes are not shown to cover that failure mode directly.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both PRs address blocking/backpressure caused by the write_stream memory object stream being created with buffer size 0 in stdio_server(). A size-0 (rendezvous) channel forces send() to block until stdout_writer is ready to receive, which causes a handler trying to queue a final response to block while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 exposes read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as caller-supplied parameters (default 0, so out-of-the-box behavior is unchanged and callers must know to opt in). #2654 hardcodes the write_stream buffer to 1, fixing the blocking behavior by default, and ships a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the progress-notification-blocks-response scenario.

clusters.pick_reason: 3041's parser (_split_www_authenticate_segments + _extract_bearer_auth_params) explicitly identifies the Bearer challenge by its scheme token before collecting params, so it correctly excludes params belonging to a different challenge when a header contains multiple comma-separated challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer realm=y'). 3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips text up to the first space and treats everything after as one flat param list, which does not isolate the Bearer challenge in multi-challenge headers, making it a narrower fix for the same root cause.

members.title: fix(auth): match complete WWW-Authenticate parameters
members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3041: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: the WWW-Authenticate header was parsed with naive string/regex matching that didn't respect quoted values or comma boundaries, causing substring matches on parameter/scheme names (e.g. matching part of a param name, or picking up params across different auth-scheme challenges) instead of matching complete, correctly-scoped tokens. Both add a quote-aware, comma-splitting parser to replace the old approach, touching the exact same function/region of the same file and would conflict on merge.
